lessons.title: Tracking Work and Planning Ahead
lessons.objective: Learners will understand and use keep track of and take into account in workplace and everyday contexts.

reading.text: Our team will keep track of customer requests during the software trial. We need to take into account the time required to train new staff before setting a launch date. The project manager will share a short progress report every Friday.

sentences.text: Our team will keep track of customer requests during the software trial.
We need to take into account the time required to train new staff before setting a launch date.
The project manager will share a short progress report every Friday.

targets.meaningEn: to stay informed about something by monitoring it over time
targets.meaningVi: theo dõi để nắm được thông tin cập nhật về điều gì

targets.meaningEn: to consider something when making a decision or plan
targets.meaningVi: cân nhắc, tính đến điều gì khi đưa ra quyết định hoặc kế hoạch

exercises.prompt: In the sentence 'Our team will keep track of customer requests during the software trial,' what does 'keep track of' mean?

options.text: It means to monitor customer requests and stay informed about them over time.
options.explanation: Correct: The team monitors customer requests to stay aware of them; making written records is one possible method, not part of the required meaning.

options.text: It means to ignore customer requests and forget them quickly.
options.explanation: Wrong: Ignoring requests is the opposite of monitoring them and staying informed. Written records are optional.

options.text: It means to finish customer requests in one day without taking notes.
options.explanation: Wrong: Completing requests is different from monitoring them over time; the phrase does not require written notes.

exercises.explanation: Keep track of means monitoring something to stay informed about it, as the team does with customer requests.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'keep track of' correctly and naturally.

options.text: He keeps track on his working hours in a spreadsheet every week.
options.explanation: This is wrong because it uses the incorrect preposition on instead of of.

options.text: He keeps track of his working hours in a spreadsheet every week.
options.explanation: Correct: He monitors his working hours; the spreadsheet is one way of keeping track of them.

options.text: He keeps track his working hours in a spreadsheet every week.
options.explanation: Wrong: The fixed expression is keep track of something; of is missing before his working hours.

exercises.explanation: Only b uses keep track of; a substitutes on for of, and c omits of.

exercises.prompt: In the sentence 'We need to take into account the time required to train new staff before setting a launch date,' what does 'take into account' mean?

options.text: It means to ignore the training time and set the date immediately.
options.explanation: This is wrong because ignoring is the opposite of considering something in a plan.

options.text: It means to finish the training in a few minutes without planning.
options.explanation: This is wrong because it describes speed rather than considering a factor in a decision.

options.text: It means to consider the training time when making the launch plan.
options.explanation: This is correct because it matches considering something when making a decision or plan.

exercises.explanation: Only option C reflects considering training time when planning.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'take into account' correctly and naturally.

options.text: Please take into account the travel time when you plan your commute.
options.explanation: This is correct because it means considering travel time when making a plan.

options.text: Please take into account of the travel time when you plan your commute.
options.explanation: This is wrong because it adds the extra preposition of after the fixed phrase.

options.text: Please take account into the travel time when you plan your commute.
options.explanation: Wrong: The fixed expression has the order take into account, not take account into.

exercises.explanation: Only a uses take into account with the correct order and without an extra of.

exercises.prompt: You are texting a friend who wants to buy a new laptop for college. Write 2-3 sentences giving friendly advice about what to consider. Use the phrase 'take into account'.
exercises.sampleAnswer: If you buy a laptop for college, you should take into account the battery life and weight. A lighter model with a long battery will be much easier to carry to classes.
selfCheck: I used the exact phrase 'take into account'.
I wrote 2-3 sentences as friendly advice, not a workplace report.
I clearly state what factor should be considered.
